verification.reason: The claim's premise is wrong. The test file is packages/evals/test/parity.test.ts, and line 978 has `await expect(measure(env, runners())).rejects.toThrow(/EEXIST/)`. A symlink planted at the temp path makes save() fail on `writeFileSync(..., {flag:"wx"})` with EEXIST, which is not a LostLock. That error goes through the `throw thrown` rethrow at parity.ts:437. With `if (false) throw thrown;` measureParity would return 2 and the rejection assertion would fail, so the mutant is caught. The claim's own scenario, `range` throwing Error("boom"), would never reach that line: parity.ts:838-841 catches range errors and records them as an attempt.

The trace holds. `checkoutCommit` (lines 1009-1020) resolves only `dirname(path)`, so a final-component link to a file inside the checkout is not caught. At line 647 it is passed `[out, MELIAN_EVAL_MISSES]` as given. Then `ResultsLock.take` (463-470) calls `realpathSync(out)`, which follows the final link. Line 663 sets `out = held.lock.file`, the in-checkout target. After that, `save` (713-718) writes `<target>.<pid>.tmp` and renames it over the target. The stores directory at line 800 and the lock file also land in the checkout. In base, `out` stayed the link's own path. Saving renamed over the link itself, and the stores sat beside the link outside the checkout. Base `checkoutCommit` (the base search found only the dirname resolution at line 896) had the same gap but did no damage. The head's new link-following turns that gap into writes inside the checkout. Those writes dirty the tree, so later resumes fail at the status check, and a tracked target gets overwritten. This breaks the guideline's "through a symbolic link or not" refusal before any model is paid for.
